rationale: All five scientific endpoints (analyses A-E) are correctly covered by named checks matching the declared output paths and schemas; the reference is reproducible (byte-identical repeats) and independently cross-validated (independent solution matched all 2059 cells, max relative difference 0); the 1e-9 + 1e-9*|ref| tolerance is publicly disclosed, calibrated against alternate decimal spellings, and validated by passing reference/recomputed/alternative controls; endpoint recovery for A and B followed the permitted faithful-recomputation route; and the three asset-value hints were each inspected in installed test source and judged unrelated rounded spot-check constants of differently-configured regression runs. However, acceptance is blocked by executed control failures caused by grader and probe defects: (1) Time-cell mismatches are attributed only to the structural check and never fail the per-file value checks whose public text declares Time comparison, so probes 'dcd-time-offset-omitted' and 'time-sign-flip-ca-table' recorded passed_control=false; (2) the valid-alternative probe 'tolerance-midpoint-encoding' failed because it shifted the Frame column itself, violating the exact-ordinal Frame rule it meant to preserve. Repair the grader so Time comparisons feed each per-file value-check decision and fix the representation probe to leave Frame untouched, then re-execute all controls on the new candidate.

comparisons.rationale: The five endpoints' numeric content is scientifically sound and independently validated, but the comparison contract has a check-attribution defect: Time cells are publicly declared to be part of each per-file value comparison, yet the implementation routes Time failures exclusively into the structural check, leaving the named value checks passing on submissions with wrong Time values. This permissive rule at the check level caused two executed wrong-solution probes to record failed controls and conflicts with the published check descriptions.
